column3: “Rulers” is rendered “lords,” and “at the last” as “in the rear.”
NASB supplies “doing here” and “no fault”; “these days or these years” is rendered “these days, or rather these years.” “The day he fell” becomes “the day he deserted to me.”
“Send back the man” is rendered “Make the man go back,” and NASB adds “or” and “For.”
Close to the Hebrew; “struck down” is rendered “slain.”
“In the camp” is rendered “in the army,” and “not good” as “not pleasing.”
“Do not do evil in the eyes of” is rendered “that you may not displease.”
“When I was before you” is rendered “when I came before you.”
“Good in my eyes” is rendered “pleasing in my sight.”
